verdict: This is the same family as the onboarding — the cream, the didone numerals, the ledger rows and the eyebrow discipline all hold — but it still reads engineered, because no wall commits to one work: Home hangs its signature line at half ink above a louder 68pt "860" wearing two caption lines and a dark camera disc, the evening close stacks five registers into an intake form, and becoming, the emotional center, is wall text floating over a 55% vacant page with not one photograph hung anywhere in the show. The benchmark's rule is one work, full ink, one caption, composed emptiness; these walls each carry two works, three captions, and dead emptiness that reads as unfinished rather than curated. Designed is close — the materials are right; what is missing is commitment of scale and the arrival of art.

compositions.composition: THE SIGNED PAGE. Top band: 13pt tracked date eyebrow, one 24pt outline menu glyph, nothing else. The upper wall is the checklist as a ledger of kept lines: each act of the day is ONE 56–64pt cocoa serif line (two lines of type allowed), 28pt of air between acts, each closed by a full-width hairline with a 28pt hollow seal sitting ON the rule at the right margin — open lines at full ink, waiting. "860" moves down to lead the foot ledger at 34pt didone ("so far — 860 of ~1,473"), with overnight fast and steps as the two quiet rows beneath, exactly the beat-19 grammar. The lower third holds one object only: yesterday's best plate photograph as a ~140pt tipped-in swatch, square-cornered, 13pt caption — the first art in the show, anchoring the void so the emptiness reads composed, not vacant.

ONE QUESTION IN THE DARKENING ROOM. Delete the form. The wall: eyebrow, then "how did today feel?" set as the work at ~56pt serif high on the page; beneath a single full-width hairline, the three answers as bare serif words — proud · okay · tender — at 26–28pt in one spaced line; tapping one inks it rose and stamps the day's seal on the rule. The foot carries the ledger only: protein 62 of 90g, tomorrow: a balanced day. "best plate today?" survives as a 17pt italic whisper above the ledger that opens jeni. Warm the cream 2% after sunset. One work, one gesture, done.

THE COVER GETS ITS IMAGE. Masthead "becoming" drops to 24pt italic running head with the 11pt week eyebrow beneath; her best plate photograph of the week runs FULL-BLEED, edge to edge with no radius, from under the masthead to ~60% of page height — art paper, tipped in. The cover line sits on the lower cream at 56–64pt over up to three lines: "this week: protein earlier in the day." One 19pt grey caption line only; the cycle note and the talk-through link move to interior pages. Foot: 3pt ink page-mark, 1pt neighbors, "1 — 12" folio. No-photo weeks run the Vogue text-only cover: the line alone at 72pt in the void — which is what this page almost is now, but committed.

(All three becoming captures show the cover — the pager never advanced; re-capture before sign-off. Composed from the locked materials:) THE DATUM AS THE PLATE. Each interior spread hangs one number as the work: the weight page sets "74.2" at 96–120pt didone left of center with "kg · monday" in 17pt italic hung off its baseline, and the 7-day trend drawn as ONE 2pt rose thread beneath — no axes, no grid, no dots — entering from the left bleed and exiting the right so the next page continues the same thread, a stitch through the whole book. The pacing page enlarges the mounds figure to ~55% of page height, morning mound inked rose where the protein should move, one caption line. Every spread: running head and folio at identical positions, one work, wall text never over two lines.

(Un-witnessed — the once-a-day gate held; it must be re-captured.) THE COLOPHON PAGE. Full cream, no tab bar, no chrome, nothing to operate. "monday, july 27" in the 13pt eyebrow; the letter set at 24–28pt serif, 1.6 leading, six lines maximum, ragged right, 32pt margins, opening with her name. At the foot, jeni signs with a single rose seal and a 13pt ghost line — "tap to keep it." It should land exactly like beat 21 of onboarding: one address centered in vast cream, the most expensive page in the app because it carries the least.

checklist_iconic.diagnosis: The kept line is one faded serif line at half ink with an apologetic caption, out-shouted by the 68pt numeral below it and the dark camera disc above it — nothing on the wall says "this is the work." Worse, its half-ink open state reads as done-and-dimmed rather than waiting, so the page never visibly asks to be completed; a screenshot of this screen today is a screenshot of the 860.
checklist_iconic.proposal: THE LEDGER SHE SIGNS. The checklist becomes the entire upper wall: every act of the day is one 56–64pt full-cocoa serif line closed by a full-width hairline with a 28pt hollow rose seal sitting on the rule at the right margin — an unsigned contract line, the page visibly waiting. Keeping a line does not check or dim it; it SIGNS it: the hairline redraws itself left to right (0.4s trim), the seal fills rose and stamps with one soft haptic, and a 13pt italic plate mark appears under the rule at the right — "kept · 7:41 pm." Maximum three lines a day, largest first; the day's final signature pulls the existing Metal silk sweep once along its hairline. The screenshot is a page of signed serif lines with rose seals and timestamps — a contract with herself, legible at thumbnail size, and ownable: no one else ships a signature ledger as a checklist.

becoming_pageturn: Pages behave as sheets, not slides, using .scrollTransition phases: the running head (masthead + eyebrow) and folio are FIXED at identical positions on every page — the book's constant — while each page's interior plane translates at ~0.92x of scroll offset (12pt of interior parallax) and a 1pt fore-edge shadow at the leading edge deepens mid-drag and releases at commit, the physics of paper lifting without any 3D rotation. Continuity makes it printed: the full-width hairlines and the 2pt rose trend thread run to both bleeds so every page literally continues the previous page's lines, and the fore-edge ticks at the foot slide beneath a fixed seal bookmark, current page a 3pt ink bar. Type settles rather than travels — headlines fade in from 0.97 scale with zero vertical motion — while art (photo, thread, mounds) carries the parallax. Pacing is darkness and light: alternate dense pages (full-bleed photograph, figure spreads) with near-empty ones (a single 96pt number; a one-line week verdict), so the swipe rhythm itself feels like leafing. The turn ends with an 80ms interactiveSpring overshoot on the parallax layer only and one soft haptic tick as the sheet seats itself.
one_move: Rebuild Home's upper wall as the signed ledger at full ink and full scale: each act of the day one 56–64pt cocoa serif line over a full-width hairline with a hollow rose seal, signed when kept (rule redraws, seal fills and stamps, 13pt plate-mark timestamp), with "860" demoted to lead the foot ledger at 34pt. It makes the signature the largest, darkest object on the most-seen wall, gives the open day a visible state of waiting, and flips the app's identity in one stroke from beautiful stat sheet to a page she signs — the screenshot the founder is asking for.
